The original managed-file fixture exercised ten intentional apply/idempotency
failures across both backends, including four under the pinned controller.
Two additional literal V1 mismatch arms proved L5 failure and rollback with retained row diagnostics.
Eighteen effective recovery probes checked restored content or file absence. Same-path
success → failure → success invalidated and then restored its latest pointer.
Different-path failures preserved the unrelated successful pointer. Every
intermediate record and pointer was captured before overwrite.

The separate literal-copy/V1 fixture passed fresh single-VM and two-node full
chains through the pinned OCI controller. Its unchanged generated records
passed both local and production remote-adapter target gates after genuine
pure base imports of documentation and an unimported Go package, without a
second target run or a manual execution-path list. Changed scoped blob/mode,
an upstream change to executed Go, new matching plugin/vars members and changed controller lock each failed for
the expected scope or membership reason. The remote adapter received complete
responses derived from the real scratch Git graph; this was not live GitHub.

Native successful records retained valid schemas/outcomes/statuses with supported
inline api_token values v1, success, pass and git. The first controlled single
chain scans public fixture/version output containing the same short literals;
reported matches remain visible in the table and original records.
No raw step output is committed. The first controlled single
chain also ignored hostile ambient Ansible configuration/plugin paths and
Python startup code. A further effective-state probe confirmed fixture content.
Final ephemeral cleanup and teardown removed only PR225 targets; existing
user VMs were preserved.

Raw stdout/stderr, per-arm records/pointers, frozen driver, actual-record hashes
and the complete local/remote adapter receipts remain separate verification artifacts.

Ansible, verification, idempotency, publication and libvirt recovery. It does
not validate production roles, service upgrades or cross-version migrations.
The static candidate binary came from an isolated Git archive with explicit
candidate/tree flags and VCS stamping disabled.

literal execution grammar. Ambient execution and unsupported inputs remain

source/binary provenance cannot qualify. Resolver version 10 rejects older proofs.

assembly is eligible only within the bounded native include audit. Arbitrary
